Dispersionless (or quasi-classical) limits of [[integrable]] [[partial differential equations]] (PDE)  arise in various problems of mathematics and physics and have been intensively studied in recent literature (see e.g. [[#References|references]] below). They typically arise when considering slowly modulated long waves of an integrable dispersive PDE system.

==Examples==

===Dispersionless KP equation===
The dispersionless [[Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation]] (dKPE), also known (up to an inessential linear change of variables) as the [[List of nonlinear partial differential equations#G–K|Khokhlov–Zabolotskaya equation]], has the form

:<math> (u_t+uu_{x})_x+u_{yy}=0,\qquad (1)</math>
It arises from the commutation
:<math> [L_1, L_2]=0.\qquad (2)</math>
of the following pair of 1-parameter families of vector fields
:<math> L_1=\partial_y+\lambda\partial_x-u_x\partial_{\lambda},\qquad (3a)</math>
:<math> L_2=\partial_t+(\lambda^2+u)\partial_x+(-\lambda u_x+u_y)\partial_{\lambda},\qquad (3b)</math>
where <math> \lambda</math> is a spectral parameter. The dKPE is the <math>x</math>-dispersionless limit of the celebrated [[Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation]], arising when considering long waves of that system. The dKPE, like many other (2+1)-dimensional integrable dispersionless systems,  admits a (3+1)-dimensional generalization.<ref name=AS>{{cite journal |doi=10.1007/s11005-017-1013-4|arxiv=1401.2122|title=New integrable (3 + 1)-dimensional systems and contact geometry |year=2018 |last1=Sergyeyev |first1=A. |s2cid=119159629 |journal=Letters in Mathematical Physics |volume=108 |issue=2 |pages=359–376 |bibcode=2018LMaPh.108..359S }}</ref>

===The Benney moment equations===
The dispersionless KP system is closely related to the [[David Benney|Benney]] moment hierarchy, each of which is a dispersionless integrable system:
:<math> A^n_{t_2} + A^{n+1}_x + n A^{n-1} A^0_x =0. </math>
These arise as the consistency condition between
:<math> \lambda = p + \sum_{n=0}^\infty A^n/p^{n+1}, </math>
and the simplest two evolutions in the hierarchy are:
:<math> p_{t_2} + p p_x + A^0_x =0, </math>
:<math> p_{t_3}  + p^2 p_x + (p A^0+A^1)_x = 0, </math>

The dKP is recovered on setting 
:<math> u = A^0, </math>
and eliminating the other moments, as well as identifying <math>y=t_2</math> and <math>t= t_3</math>.

If one sets <math>A^n = h v^n</math>, so that the countably many moments <math>A^n</math> are expressed in terms of just two functions, the classical [[shallow water equations]] result:
:<math>h_y + (hv)_x=0,</math>
:<math>v_y +v v_x + h_x=0.</math>
These may also be derived from considering slowly modulated wave train solutions of the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]]. Such 'reductions', expressing the moments in terms of finitely many dependent variables, are described by the [[Gibbons-Tsarev equation]].

===Dispersionless Korteweg–de Vries equation===
The dispersionless [[Korteweg–de Vries equation]] (dKdVE) reads as

:<math> u_{t_3}=uu_{x}.\qquad (4)</math>

It is the dispersionless or quasiclassical limit of the [[Korteweg–de Vries equation]].
It is satisfied by <math>t_2</math>-independent solutions of the dKP system.
It is also obtainable from the <math>t_3</math>-flow of the Benney hierarchy on setting 
:<math> \lambda^2 = p^2 + 2A^0.</math>

===Dispersionless Novikov–Veselov  equation===
The dispersionless [[Novikov-Veselov equation]] is most commonly written as the following equation for a [[real-valued function]] <math>v=v(x_1,x_2,t)</math>:
:<math>
\begin{align}
& \partial_{ t } v = \partial_{ z }( v w ) + \partial_{ \bar z }( v \bar w ), \\
& \partial_{ \bar z } w = - 3 \partial_{ z } v,
\end{align}
</math>

where the following standard notation of [[complex analysis]] is used: <math> \partial_{ z } = \frac{ 1 }{ 2 } ( \partial_{ x_1 } - i \partial_{ x_2 } ) </math>, <math> \partial_{ \bar z } = \frac{ 1 }{ 2 } ( \partial_{ x_1 } + i \partial_{ x_2 } ) </math>. The function <math>w</math> here is an [[auxiliary function]],  defined uniquely from <math>v</math> up to a holomorphic summand.
